Build the KV-cache bill

One token leaves a key and a value in every layer. Multiply that small record across heads, dimensions, tokens and active users—and it becomes a serving cost.

Bill for one user

6.44 GB

At 32,768 tokens, this fixed example keeps 6.44 GB of K/V history for one conversation.

32,768 token records
2 × 48 × 8 × 128 × 32,768 × 2 bytes = 6.44 GB

Bill for all active users

51.54 GB

8 private caches × 6.44 GB each. The model cannot reuse one user’s history for another user.

The serving lesson: context length sets the cache cost of one conversation; concurrency copies that cost for every active conversation. Reducing either multiplier saves memory linearly.
What this counts: raw K and V tensors for a fixed 48-layer, 8-KV-head, head-dimension-128, bf16 example—the comparison yardstick used later in this lesson. Real inference also needs model weights, activations, temporary workspaces and allocator headroom, so this is not total GPU memory.
